title: DynamoDB from C#
description: Use Amazon DynamoDB for NoSQL document storage in ASP.NET Core applications.

data.text: Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL database. It delivers single-digit millisecond performance at any scale, making it ideal for serverless applications and high-traffic workloads.

items: **Item** — a single document with attributes, similar to a row
**Attribute** — a key-value pair, similar to a column
**Partition key** — the primary key that determines data distribution
**Sort key** — optional secondary key for range queries

data.title: Create a DynamoDB table with AWS CLI
data.content:
Create a table for posts with a partition key.
# Expected output: Table is created and becomes ACTIVE within seconds.
data.code: aws dynamodb create-table --table-name Posts --attribute-definitions AttributeName=Id,AttributeType=S --key-schema AttributeName=Id,KeyType=HASH --billing-mode PAY_PER_REQUEST --region us-east-1

data.title: Build a posts API with DynamoDB
data.description: Create a minimal API that stores posts in DynamoDB.
steps: Create a DynamoDB table named `Posts` with an `Id` partition key
Create endpoints for creating, reading, and deleting posts
Test the endpoints with curl or Postman
data.expectedOutcome: Posts are stored and retrieved from DynamoDB.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: DynamoDB is a fully managed NoSQL database
Use partition keys and sort keys for efficient data access
DynamoDB scales automatically without manual intervention
data.takeaway: DynamoDB is the AWS-native NoSQL option for serverless and high-scale ASP.NET Core applications.
